source: his 2026-10-29 06:14 "are we making too many 'special' ones? Wondering how we make daily driver ones people wouldnt mind replaying", then "lets try some plain first"
_note: PLAIN 3: THE DEFENCE. Raiders keep hitting a quiet settlement and are due back. Stand with them until they give up.
A COMMON, NOT A SPECIAL: written to survive the tenth play. No reveal, no secret, no twist; the issuer has a small
ordinary stake and says it in one short line. What changes on a replay is the place, the drive and what is there
(his 09-23 'All the dials are new gameplay'). The register is his 07-31 'pure chill out Truck Simulator Dad Game
vibes', and his Goods Package (localcargo_qst09a) is the specimen. No pay promised in a voiced line (10-27).
Letters are the replay lever that exists: a b and c later, same job, other words, live side by side.
A HOLD ALONE, no machine to start first: four drafts already open on 'start a machine, then hold' (09a, 16a, 19a, 22a)
and that shape should not be the only way a fight arrives. Unproven: whether a board hold can be beat 1 with nothing
before it; the lint is the first test. Residents alive, defended. Pay: med.

place._theme: Quiet sites with residents; here they are the people being defended, so the words keep them alive.

prose.name: Defense: Raiders at the <Place> on <Planet>
prose.briefing: Raiders have hit the <Place> twice this month and they're due back. The people there would like someone with a gun to stand with them.
prose.card: Defense contract. Raiders are expected to attack the <Place> on <Planet>. Hold the site until they withdraw. Payment on contract completion.

beats.journal: Raiders came at the <Place> three times. I held it with the people who live there until they gave up.
say: That's them off. They'll think twice before they come back, and we might get a proper night's sleep.

broadcast: They've hit us twice this month and they'll be back tonight. We'll do what we can, but we need someone who can shoot to stand with us.
_speech: Tired, practical. The technician's voice from 54a; his ear decides.
